question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution:
The correct answer is '**gave up**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase refers to Ms Navalnaya leaving her career to focus on raising her children, which implies a voluntary decision to stop working.
 
• The phrasal verb "**gave up**" means to voluntarily quit or stop doing something. (त्याग देना)
 
• In the context, “she gave up her job” clearly communicates the intended meaning of her leaving her profession.
 
• Other options are contextually incorrect: 
 
 
• **Keep back** – (रोकना): Means to restrain or hold something back; does not fit.
 
• **Broke down** – (टूटना): Usually refers to emotional collapse or mechanical failure.
 
• **Brought about** – (लाना): Means to cause or initiate a change; unrelated to resigning or quitting.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

Complete Sentence: *As economics graduate, she had a career in banking but **gave up**__ her job to bring up their two children when Alexei rose to prominence as an opposition politician.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Keep back** – (रोकना): Implies physical or emotional restraint.

 **Example:** He couldn’t keep back his tears.
 
• **Broke down** – (टूटना): Typically used for emotional collapse or when a machine stops functioning.

 **Example:** The car broke down on the highway.
 
• **Brought about** – (लाना): Means to cause something to happen.

 **Example:** The new policy brought about major changes in the system.
